- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 2–3 days post-spike.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, consider mean reversion bias — reduce forecast by 1–4% for next 3–5 days unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 3–5 days, model often lags; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% in next 2–3 days to capture sentiment momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, if model consistently forecasts >70% above recent 18-day average, apply downward bias correction (−2–5%) to reflect volatility and sentiment decay.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/− cycles (e.g., +0.67, -0.00, +0.33), model often misaligns with sentiment direction; adjust forecast to match sentiment trend direction, not historical mean.
